meta.title: The Story of the Farmer
meta.verseText: You are the children that God dearly loves. So follow his example. Lead a life of love, just as Christ did.
meta.theme: God's Word is like seed, and our hearts are like soil. When we hear God's Word and do what it says, God's Kingdom grows in us and through us.

questions.text: Who did Jesus talk about in this story that scattered seed?
questions.hint: This person plants seeds in a field.
questions.explanation: Jesus told a story about a farmer who went out to scatter seed on his field.

questions.text: In Jesus' story, what does the seed stand for?
questions.hint: It is something we hear and can grow in our hearts.
questions.explanation: Jesus explained that the seed is like God's Word being planted in people's hearts.

questions.text: In the story, what do the different kinds of soil stand for?
questions.hint: It is the place where the seed of God's Word can grow.
questions.explanation: The soil is like our hearts, and how ready they are to receive and grow God's Word.

questions.text: Which book of the Bible tells the Story of the Farmer?
questions.hint: It is one of the first four books of the New Testament.
questions.explanation: The parable of the farmer (or sower) is found in Matthew 13:1-23.

questions.text: What happened to the seed that fell on the hard path?
options: It did not really take root
questions.hint: The ground was too hard for it to sink in.
questions.explanation: Seed on the hard path is like a heart that does not really listen, so God's Word does not take root.

questions.text: What was the problem with the seed that fell on rocky soil?
options: It had no roots and gave up when things got hard
questions.hint: It grew fast but could not last when trouble came.
questions.explanation: The rocky soil is like hearing God's Word with excitement but giving up when things get hard, because there are no deep roots.

questions.text: What crowded out the seed that fell among the thorns?
questions.hint: These are the busy, stressful things that pull our attention away.
questions.explanation: The thorns are like worries and distractions that crowd out God's Word in our hearts.

questions.text: What happened to the seed that landed on good soil?
options: It grew and produced a big crop
questions.hint: This is the best result of all!
questions.explanation: The seed on good soil grew and produced a big crop, showing a heart that hears God's Word and acts on it.

questions.text: What does the 'good soil' heart do with God's Word?
options: Hears it and does something with it
questions.hint: It doesn't just listen; it takes action.
questions.explanation: The good soil is the heart that hears God's Word and does something with it, so God's Kingdom grows.

questions.text: What big idea was Jesus teaching about with this story?
questions.hint: It can start in small ways that are easy to miss.
questions.explanation: Jesus used the farmer story to help people understand God's Kingdom and how it grows.

questions.text: Jesus taught that God's Kingdom can start in ways that seem small and easy to miss.
questions.hint: Think of a tiny seed growing into something big.
questions.explanation: True! Jesus taught that God's Kingdom can start small, like a seed, and grow into something much bigger.

questions.text: The farmer only threw seed in one small spot.
questions.hint: The lesson says the farmer scattered seed everywhere.
questions.explanation: False! The farmer scattered seed everywhere, and it landed on many kinds of ground.

questions.text: A seed looks tiny, but with the right soil, water, and sunlight it can grow into something much bigger.
questions.hint: Think about how a plant starts.
questions.explanation: True! A tiny seed can grow into something big, just like a small act of faith can grow in God's Kingdom.

questions.text: The rocky-soil heart keeps following God even when life gets hard.
questions.hint: Remember, the rocky soil had no roots.
questions.explanation: False! The rocky-soil heart gives up when things get hard because it has no deep roots.

questions.text: Our memory verse tells us to follow God's example and lead a life of love.
questions.hint: Think about Ephesians 5:1-2a.
questions.explanation: True! Ephesians 5:1-2a tells us to follow God's example and lead a life of love, just as Christ did.

questions.text: Worries and distractions have no effect on how God's Word grows in us.
questions.hint: Remember what the thorns did.
questions.explanation: False! Worries and distractions are like thorns that can crowd out God's Word in our hearts.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: 'The seed is like God's ______.'
questions.hint: It is what we read in the Bible.
questions.explanation: The seed is like God's Word, which is scattered into people's hearts.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: 'The soil is like our ______.'
questions.hint: It is the part of us that listens to God.
questions.explanation: The soil is like our hearts, showing how ready we are to receive God's Word.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: 'Ask God to help your heart be like ______ soil.'
questions.hint: It is the soil that grows a big crop.
questions.explanation: We want our hearts to be like good soil: ready to listen, grow, and do what God says.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: 'You are the children that God dearly ______.'
questions.hint: It is how God feels about you in the memory verse.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 5:1 says, 'You are the children that God dearly loves.'

questions.text: Fill in the blank: 'Lead a life of ______, just as Christ did.'
questions.hint: Christ showed us this by how He treated people.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 5:2a tells us to lead a life of love, just as Christ did.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: 'The good soil is the heart that hears God's Word and ______ something with it.'
questions.hint: It takes action instead of just listening.
questions.explanation: The good-soil heart hears God's Word and does something with it, letting God's Kingdom grow.

questions.text: You hear God's Word at church and feel excited, but by the next day you forget it because you never think about it again. Which soil is that like?
questions.hint: This soil grows fast but has no roots.
questions.explanation: That is like the rocky soil, which grows fast but has no roots and does not last.

questions.text: What is one way you could be like 'good soil' this week?
options: Hear God's Word and do what it says
questions.hint: Good soil takes action.
questions.explanation: Being like good soil means hearing God's Word and actually doing what it says, like showing kindness and love.

questions.text: The lesson asks, 'Can you spread seeds?' What does spreading seeds mean for us?
options: Sharing God's love and goodness with others
questions.hint: It is about showing God's Kingdom to people around you.
questions.explanation: Spreading seeds means sharing God's love and goodness so His Kingdom grows in others too.

questions.text: According to the memory verse, we should imitate God. What does 'imitate' mean?
options: To copy or follow someone's example
questions.hint: Think about copying what someone else does.
questions.explanation: To imitate means to copy or follow someone's example. We imitate God by walking in love like Christ did.

questions.text: The Conversation Starter asks: 'What are you going to do with what you have ______?'
questions.hint: It is about God's Word going into your ears and heart.
questions.explanation: The Conversation Starter asks what you will do with what you have heard, encouraging us to act like good soil.

questions.text: When you picture a 'kingdom,' the lesson says you might imagine castles and crowns. But God's Kingdom often starts how?
questions.hint: Think of a tiny seed.
questions.explanation: God's Kingdom often starts in ways that seem small and easy to miss, like a tiny seed that grows.

questions.text: Which of these is a small thing that can make a big difference, according to the lesson?
questions.hint: It is something nice you can say to someone.
questions.explanation: The lesson says small things like a kind word, a good choice, or a seed can make a big difference.

questions.text: How does God's Kingdom grow, based on this lesson?
options: In us and through us when we hear and obey God's Word
By keeping God's Word to ourselves
questions.hint: It grows both inside you and out to others.
questions.explanation: God's Kingdom grows in us and through us when we hear God's Word and do something with it.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: 'So follow his ______,' says the memory verse about God.
questions.hint: It means to do what He does.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 5:1 says to follow God's example by leading a life of love.

questions.text: A friend is being left out at recess. What is a 'good soil' choice you could make?
options: Invite them to play and show God's love
questions.hint: Think about walking in love, like the memory verse says.
questions.explanation: Inviting the friend to play shows God's love in action, which is what a good-soil heart does with God's Word.

story.summary: Jesus sat by a lake and taught a big crowd using a story about a farmer. The farmer scattered seed all over his field. Some seed fell on the hard path, some on rocky ground, some among thorns, and some on good soil. Only the seed in good soil grew and produced a big crop. Jesus explained that the seed is like God's Word and the soil is like our hearts. A hard heart does not listen, a rocky heart gives up when things get tough, and a thorny heart gets crowded by worries. But a good-soil heart hears God's Word and does something with it, and that is how God's Kingdom grows in us and through us. Our memory verse reminds us to follow God's example and lead a life of love, just as Christ did.

scenes.title: Jesus Teaches About a Farmer
scenes.description: By the lake, Jesus tells a crowd a story about a farmer who goes out to scatter seed. He is really teaching them about God's Kingdom, which can start small like a tiny seed and grow into something big.

scenes.title: Seed on the Path and the Rocks
scenes.description: Some seed lands on the hard path where it cannot take root, and some lands on rocky soil where it grows fast but withers because it has no roots. These are like hearts that do not listen or give up when things get hard.

scenes.title: Seed Among the Thorns
scenes.description: Other seed falls among thorns, where worries and distractions grow up and crowd it out. This is like a heart that gets too busy and stressed to let God's Word grow.

scenes.title: Seed in Good Soil
scenes.description: At last some seed lands on good soil and grows into a big crop. This is the heart that hears God's Word and does something with it, so God's Kingdom grows in us and through us.

scenes.title: Grow and Go: Living It Out
scenes.description: Jesus wants us to be like good soil this week. Our memory verse tells us to imitate God and lead a life of love, spreading seeds of goodness to everyone around us.
